How to calculate income tax and take-home pay in Portugal (2026)

Portugal taxes residents on worldwide income with nine progressive IRS bands from 12.2% to 48%, and employees pay 11% social security on top. This page models mainland Portugal. On a €30,000 salary a resident pays about €7,750 in social security and IRS and keeps about €22,250, or 74.2% of gross. A non-resident pays a flat 25% and keeps about €19,200, while a young worker in year one of IRS Jovem keeps about €26,700.

What the law says

The figures below are the 2026 rates as the calculator models them, for a full-year employee on mainland Portugal. Which rules apply depends on whether you are a tax resident. As a rule you are resident if you spend more than 183 days in Portugal in a twelve-month period or have a home there that you keep as your habitual residence, and residents are taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxed only on Portuguese income.

IRS scale for residents

The scale applies to taxable income, which is your salary minus the specific deduction for employees (the greater of €4,587.09 and your social security) and, at low incomes, the subsistence minimum (mínimo de existência). Deductions from the tax itself, such as the standard €250 the calculator applies and family and expense deductions, are then taken off the result. A solidarity surcharge of 2.5% applies to taxable income between €80,000 and €250,000 and 5% above.

Social security

Employees pay 11% of gross salary and the employer pays 23.75% on top, which is not part of your take-home pay. The calculator shows the employer share as a separate line beside your net.

IRS Jovem

IRS Jovem exempts part of a young worker's employment income from IRS for the first ten years of work. The calculator models the exempt share by year: 100% in year 1, 75% in years 2 to 4, 50% in years 5 to 7 and 25% in years 8 to 10, up to a cap of €29,542.15 of exempt income. The regime has conditions on age, qualifications and when you started work, so check eligibility before relying on it. The calculator does not test them.

IFICI, the successor to the NHR regime

The IFICI regime (the tax incentive for scientific research and innovation) replaced the non-habitual resident (NHR) regime for new arrivals. The calculator models a flat 20% on employment income, with social security on top. It is meant for people in qualifying roles, such as research, higher education, certain technology and innovation activities, who were not recently Portuguese tax residents, and it runs for a limited number of years. The exact conditions are strict, so confirm them with the tax authority or an adviser.

Non-resident rate

A non-resident employed in Portugal pays a flat 25% on Portuguese employment income, with no scale and no deductions. The calculator applies 25% of gross and adds social security.

How much tax and take-home pay on €30,000 in Portugal?

This is a resident employee on €30,000. Social security takes €3,300 (11%). The specific deduction is €4,587, so taxable income is about €25,413. The progressive scale on that amount gives about €4,700, and the standard €250 deduction from the tax brings it to €4,450. You keep about €22,250, or 74.2% of gross.

  1. Gross paya year, before tax€30,000
  2. Social security (11%)contribution, taken from pay−€3,300
  3. Employer social security (23.75%), on toppaid by the employer, on top€7,125
  4. Specific deductionlowers the taxable income€4,587
  5. IRS, after deductions from taxtax, taken from pay−€4,450
  6. Deductions from tax (family expenses)credit, already inside the tax€250
  7. Take-home pay74.2% of gross, €1,854 a month€22,250

Your marginal rate is 41.6%: the next euro is taxed in the 30.6% IRS band, and social security takes another 11% of it. The employer's 23.75% (€7,125) is paid on top of your gross.

How IRS Jovem changes take-home pay on €30,000 in year one

A young worker in year 1 of IRS Jovem has 100% of the salary exempt up to the €29,542 cap, so almost all of the €30,000 is exempt. What remains is below the specific deduction, so IRS is nil. Only social security (€3,300) is paid, and you keep about €26,700, or 89.0% of gross.

  1. Gross paya year, before tax€30,000
  2. Social security (11%)contribution, taken from pay−€3,300
  3. Employer social security (23.75%), on toppaid by the employer, on top€7,125
  4. IRS Jovem exempt share (year 1, 100%)lowers the taxable income€29,542
  5. Specific deductionlowers the taxable income€4,587
  6. IRS, after deductions from taxtax, taken from pay€0
  7. Deductions from tax (family expenses)credit, already inside the tax€0
  8. Take-home pay89.0% of gross, €2,225 a month€26,700

The marginal rate is 11.0%, which is just social security. The exempt share falls in later years, so take-home pay will drop as the regime steps down to 75%, then 50%, then 25%.

Portugal tax on €70,000 under the IFICI 20% regime

Under IFICI the calculator applies a flat 20% to a €70,000 salary, which is €14,000, with €7,700 of social security. You keep about €48,300, or 69.0% of gross. The marginal rate is 31.0%.

  1. Gross paya year, before tax€70,000
  2. Social security (11%)contribution, taken from pay−€7,700
  3. Employer social security (23.75%), on toppaid by the employer, on top€16,625
  4. IRS, IFICI regime (20% flat)tax, taken from pay−€14,000
  5. Take-home pay69.0% of gross, €4,025 a month€48,300

The flat 20% beats the resident scale most clearly at higher salaries, where the standard scale reaches 44.6% and 48%. It is a qualifying-activity regime, so check that your role and your situation fit before assuming it applies.

Portuguese tax for a non-resident employee on €30,000

A non-resident on €30,000 pays a flat 25% (€7,500) and social security of €3,300. There is no specific deduction and no scale. You keep about €19,200, or 64.0% of gross, compared with €22,250 for a resident on the same salary, which is about €3,050 less.

  1. Gross paya year, before tax€30,000
  2. Social security (11%)contribution, taken from pay−€3,300
  3. Employer social security (23.75%), on toppaid by the employer, on top€7,125
  4. IRS, non-resident (25% flat)tax, taken from pay−€7,500
  5. Take-home pay64.0% of gross, €1,600 a month€19,200

The marginal rate is 36.0% (25% plus 11% social security). If you are going to be in Portugal long enough to count as resident, the resident scale is usually cheaper at this income.

How to pay less tax, legally

These are mainstream, legal ways to reduce Portuguese tax. Which ones apply depends on your residence, age and role.

Make sure of your tax residence status

Suits: anyone arriving during the year. As the non-resident example shows, the flat 25% with no deductions costs more than the resident scale at moderate incomes. Registering your habitual home and keeping records of your days can matter.

Caveat: residence is decided by the tax rules, not by your visa or by what you call yourself. In your first year you may be taxed on only part of the year.

Check IRS Jovem eligibility

Suits: young employees in their first jobs, as in the year-one example. The exempt share is largest early on.

Caveat: it has conditions on age, qualifications and when you started work, and the share steps down each period. Plan for lower take-home pay in later years.

Check the IFICI regime if your role qualifies

Suits: people moving to Portugal for research, higher education or qualifying technology and innovation work, especially at higher salaries.

Caveat: the conditions on role, previous residence and employer are strict and the regime is temporary. Do not assume it applies without confirmation.

Claim expense deductions with invoices

Suits: resident employees with health, education or rent costs. A share of these costs is deducted from the tax, up to limits that depend on your income. Asking for invoices that carry your tax number (NIF) makes the expenses show up in the tax system.

Caveat: each category has its own cap, and the cap shrinks as income rises. The calculator applies them only if you enter the amounts.

Retirement savings plans

Suits: residents who want a tax benefit for long-term saving through an approved retirement savings plan (PPR).

Caveat: the benefit has limits that depend on your age, and the money is meant for retirement. Check the current rules on the tax portal. The calculator does not model it.

What the calculator does not model

  • Mainland Portugal only. The Azores and Madeira have their own reduced rates, which are not modelled.
  • Employment income only. It models one salary for a full year. It does not cover investment income, property income, self-employment or a part year.
  • No bonuses or equity. They are not modelled separately.
  • No eligibility tests. You choose resident, IRS Jovem, IFICI or non-resident. The calculator does not check age, role, residence history or days spent in Portugal.
  • Family and expense deductions are inputs. By default only the standard €250 deduction from the tax is applied. Dependants and health, education and rent costs count only if you enter them.
  • Annual figure. The result is the full-year tax, not each monthly payslip.
  • No tax treaties or foreign tax credits. Income taxed in your home country is not offset here.

General information, not tax advice. The figures follow the rules as published for the year shown. Check the ones that matter to you with the tax authority or an adviser before you sign a contract.

Frequently asked questions

How much tax do I pay on €30,000 in Portugal?

A resident employee pays about €3,300 in social security and about €4,450 in IRS, so about €7,750 in total, and keeps about €22,250. A non-resident pays a flat 25% and keeps about €19,200. Try your own figure in the Global Income Tax Calculator.

What is IFICI and is it the same as the NHR regime?

IFICI is the tax incentive for scientific research and innovation. It replaced the non-habitual resident (NHR) regime for new arrivals, and it is narrower: it is aimed at qualifying roles instead of any newcomer. The calculator models a flat 20% on employment income. The real regime has conditions on your role, your recent residence and how long it lasts, so check the Portal das Finanças before relying on it.

How does IRS Jovem reduce my tax?

IRS Jovem exempts a share of a young worker's employment income. In the calculator the share is 100% in year 1, 75% in years 2 to 4, 50% in years 5 to 7 and 25% in years 8 to 10, up to a cap on the exempt amount (€29,542.15). On €30,000 in year 1, IRS is nil and you keep €26,700. The conditions are set by the tax authority, so confirm them first.

Why is my salary paid in 14 payments in Portugal?

Portuguese employees are normally entitled to a holiday subsidy and a Christmas subsidy, each worth about a month of pay. A salary quoted as a monthly figure is therefore paid over 14 months, and some employers spread the subsidies across 12. The annual gross and the annual tax are the same either way. The calculator works on the full-year gross, so divide by 14 or 12 to match your payslips.

Why does a non-resident pay a flat 25%?

Non-residents are taxed only on Portuguese income, at a flat rate with no scale and no deductions. At €30,000 that is €7,500, about €3,050 more than a resident pays on the same salary. Becoming a tax resident, by spending enough time in Portugal or keeping a habitual home there, moves you to the progressive scale.

Do employers pay social security on top in Portugal?

Yes. You pay 11% of gross, and the employer pays 23.75% on top, which is €7,125 on a €30,000 salary. The employer share is part of what the job costs, but not of your take-home pay. The calculator lists it as a separate line.
